status_summary: The administration's main China trade tools have been the broad measures the essay argues against: Executive Order 14257 (signed 2025-04-02) set a baseline duty on all trading partners with country-specific rates, and later Section 232 and Section 301 actions apply to whole sectors or economies (see c26-02 and c26-04). Firm-level action has continued through export controls framed around national security rather than unfair trade practices: a BIS rule effective 2025-03-25 (90 FR 14046) added 11 Chinese entities and one in Taiwan to the Entity List for supporting military modernization through AI, chips and supercomputers, without citing intellectual property theft. A BIS interim final rule effective 2025-09-29 (90 FR 47201) extended Entity List restrictions to affiliates at least 50 percent owned by listed parties, and BIS suspended it on 2025-11-12 until 2026-11-09.

timeline.event: S. 330, the Combatting China's Pilfering of Intellectual Property Act, was introduced in the Senate and referred to the Foreign Relations Committee; it would require sanctions, including asset blocking and visa bars, on Chinese persons found to have engaged in a pattern of significant theft of U.S. intellectual property.
BIS added 12 entities (11 in China, 1 in Taiwan) to the Entity List, effective this date.
Executive Order 14257 (signed 2025-04-02) imposing a baseline and country-specific reciprocal tariff was published.
BIS published the Affiliates rule extending Entity List restrictions to 50 percent-owned affiliates.
BIS published a final rule suspending the affiliates rule for one year, until 2026-11-09 unless extended.

title: Target individual Chinese firms for unfair practices instead of blanket sector tariffs
uncertainties: This is a judgment call: firm-level Entity List actions against Chinese companies continue, so in_progress with a partial match is defensible; diverged is kept because the essay's central ask is firm targeting instead of blanket tariffs and the listings cite national security, not unfair trade practices. Only a few Entity List rules were read and OFAC designations were not searched. S. 330, an introduced IP-theft sanctions bill, points toward the recommendation. The Commerce Unified Agenda rule list on reginfo.gov (headed 'Agency Rule List - 2026') lists Entity List entries (0694-AK42, 0694-AK11) that state no intellectual property or unfair trade basis; the 0694-AK11 timetable shows the affiliates rule taking effect 2026-11-10. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
